core_obligations: Decompose X over the closure into two open and closed pieces and use connectedness of T over the closure to land T inside the preimage of one of them (proof lines 1028-1034).

For each quasi-compact open W, descend the two pieces to a finite Galois subextension, take the intersection over the finite Galois group of one and the union of the other to obtain Galois invariant open and closed pieces U'' and V'' with W_{k'} their disjoint union, and descend them to open and closed U_W and V_W of W (proof lines 1037-1053).

Glue the U_W and V_W over all quasi-compact opens to a decomposition of X, and check that both parts are nonempty: V locally by construction and U because it contains the image of T (proof lines 1055-1063).
proof_roadmap: Start from a decomposition over the closure and locate T in one piece (proof lines 1028-1034).
Symmetrize over a finite Galois group and descend (proof lines 1037-1053).
difficulty_reason: Let k-bar/k be a possibly infinite Galois extension, f: T to X a morphism of schemes over k; if T over the closure is connected and X over the closure is disconnected, the lemma concludes that X itself is disconnected (statement lines 1019-1025). The proof starts from a decomposition of X over the closure into two open and closed pieces and uses connectedness of T over the closure to place T entirely inside the preimage of one of them (proof lines 1028-1034). For each quasi-compact open W the two pieces descend to a finite Galois subextension k', and the author symmetrizes them over the finite Galois group to obtain Galois invariant open and closed pieces U'' and V'' of W_{k'}, which by the descent lemma come from open and closed subsets U_W and V_W of W (proof lines 1037-1053). The U_W are then glued over all quasi-compact opens using the compatibility supplied by a monotonicity statement that the author leaves as a verification, yielding a decomposition of X into two nonempty open and closed parts (proof lines 1055-1063). The claim is H2: the Galois symmetrization and the descent are the content, while the omitted compatibility is a bounded bookkeeping check.
